correctness.rationale: Let a≥b>0 be semiaxes, so circumradius R=a. The exact elliptic-integral perimeter P(a,b)=4∫_0^{π/2}√(a²sin²t+b²cos²t)dt has ∂P/∂a=4∫ a sin²t/√(...)dt<4 for finite b>0, yielding P(a,b)−λa≤(2π−λ)b for every λ≥4 with equality only a=b. A lattice-free ellipse contains the disk centered at its center with radius b, so b≤ρ(Λ), attained by deepest-hole disks. Positive/zero/negative branches and precise equality follow, and elongated ellipses inside any open lattice-free inter-row strip have P≥4a and yield infinity for λ<4. Square lattice ρ=1/√2 gives sharp √2(π−2). This derivation directly verifies all real λ thresholds, not numerical sampling.
residual_risks: Strictness relies on nondegenerate b>0; λ>2π uses shrinking disks and the supremum is never attained.

value.rationale: The motivating lattice-free perimeter–circumradius question is an explicit classical open convex-body problem. This solves a natural smooth centrally symmetric shape class sharply, gives an exact inequality strictly stronger than the general conjectured Z² value, locates two genuine λ phase boundaries and classifies all optimizers on arbitrary full-rank lattices. Despite the short calculus/geometry proof, the exact best value is not a mere parameter rename or a known-table recomputation; the lattice dependence via ρ is independently useful.
residual_risks: The elementary proof leaves priority risk in older convex-geometry sources, but elementary does not entail worthless when the exact sharp natural subproblem is not shown covered.

final_claim: For any full-rank planar lattice Λ with Euclidean covering radius ρ(Λ), lattice-free nondegenerate ellipses satisfy sup_E(P(E)−λR(E))=∞ for λ<4, (2π−λ)ρ for 4≤λ≤2π, and 0 for λ>2π, with exact optimizer classification: maximal deepest-hole disks for 4≤λ<2π, all lattice-free disks at λ=2π, and no maximizer for λ>2π.
limitations: Two-dimensional nondegenerate ellipses, Euclidean P and R only; nothing claimed for arbitrary lattice-free convex bodies.
